_readme: CANONICAL Trinidad & Tobago parameter tables. Single source of truth for BOTH the planning engine and the public calculators. Never hardcode any of these values anywhere else. Every parameter carries value + effective date + source URL + retrieved date + verification status. See README.md for the rules.
_rule: Provenance is PER-PARAMETER, not per-page. Agencies contradict themselves: NIBTT publishes benefit rates in two places with ~69% different values; the Ministry of Finance publishes a TT$30,000 cap that is two increases and 17 years out of date; the SCP application form says $4,500 where the Ministry page says $5,500. Trust the maintained page over the linked PDF, and record where each number came from.

personal_allowance.basis: s.18 Income Tax Act Chap. 75:01, as amended by Finance Act 2022
personal_allowance.notes: Also extends to non-residents receiving T&T pension income. Budget 2026 announced no further increase.

paye_bands.notes: Finance Act 2026 does not amend these. Confirmed unchanged for TY2026.

nis_deductible_portion.basis: BIR administrative practice — NO STATUTORY SECTION LOCATED
nis_deductible_portion.notes: Safe to compute with; CANNOT be cited to a section. Appears on IRD's deductions page and Form T.D.-1 but no verifier located a statutory basis. Do not claim a legal citation.

combined_deduction_cap.basis: s.28(15) Income Tax Act Chap. 75:01, raised by Finance (No. 2) Act 2021
combined_deduction_cap.warning: The Ministry of Finance annuities page STILL PUBLISHES TT$30,000. It is two increases and 17 years stale. A verification panel killed that figure 0-3. Never source this from finance.gov.tt.

first_time_homeowner.notes: Property acquired on/after 2011-01-01; claimable for five years from year of acquisition.

alimony_maintenance.notes: Lesser of payments made and the court-ordered amount.

s18D_fund_donations.basis: s.18D ITA, inserted by Finance Act 2026 cl.21(b)
s18D_fund_donations.warning: NOT a retirement provision. This is for donations to a Fund established under s.43 of the Exchequer and Audit Act Chap. 69:01. It sits BESIDE the retirement sections and shares a plausible-looking cap, which invites misreading. It has NO interaction with the combined_deduction_cap.

ordinary_rate.notes: Ordinary companies. Banks, other licensed financial institutions and petrochemical companies pay 35%.

business_levy.warning: PAYABLE ONLY WHERE IT EXCEEDS THE CORPORATION TAX LIABILITY. This is the trap for a s.134(6) illustration: a company with high turnover and thin profits pays the levy regardless, so a deduction against corporation tax may save it NOTHING. Never show a corporate tax saving without testing this.

green_fund_levy.notes: Neither deductible in computing chargeable income nor creditable against corporation tax. Unaffected by a s.134(6) contribution.

exemptions.warning: MATERIAL for a retirement app: never charge health surcharge to a 60+ client. IRD wording is 'sixty (60) years and over' (i.e. 60+); one secondary source renders it 'over 60'. IRD governs. Do NOT cross-wire with the NIS 'under 16 / 65 and over' rule — different levy.

future.warning: Rests on a Ministry of Finance budget announcement plus arithmetic (16.2 + 3). NO gazetted earnings-class schedule exists for 2027. Any 2027 class table is necessarily derived. NEVER present 2027 figures to a client as settled.

insurable_earnings_ceiling.client_insight: Earnings above this contribute at Class XVI but do NOT increase the pension. High earners hit a hard benefit ceiling. This is an honest, rules-based argument for private provision.

contribution_tables._rule: ERA-SELECTED. Contributions are computed at the rate in force WHEN THEY WERE PAID. Select by contribution date, never by claim date.

_weeks_per_year.notes: NIS is a weekly contribution; annualise at 52. Some calendar years contain 53 contribution weeks and payroll practice varies. Material only at the margin.

contribution_tables._source_note: NIBTT publishes dated sets: 1972-2006, 2008-2012, 2013-2014, 2016, 2026. The 2016 page remaining live is CORRECT — contributions paid Sept 2016 to Jan 2026 were made at 13.2%.

2026-01-05.transcription_note: Classes II-XV transcribed 2026-08-11 from NISContributions_20260105.pdf. Two independent reads of the source agreed on every cell, and both reproduced the previously-VERIFIED Class I and Class XVI rows exactly. Gates applied to all 16 rows: employee + employer = total; total / assumed_awe = 16.2%; employee share = 1/3; bands contiguous with no gaps or overlaps.
2026-01-05.client_insight: The employee pays one third. At Class XVI that is 169.50/week = 8,814.00/year, of which 70% (6,169.80) is the most NIS can ever consume of the 60,000 combined deduction cap — so a ceiling earner with no company pension has 53,830.20 of annuity room, not 60,000.

classes.class_z_correction: NIBTT's page prints 220.72. That is a typo — a stray leading '2'. Class Z is exactly 5.00% of weekly_total for every class I-XV (XV: 20.00/399.90). 414.30 x 0.05 = 20.72. DO NOT propagate NIBTT's typo.

class_z.value: employment injury coverage only, employer-paid, ~5.00% of the class weekly total
applies_to: employed person in receipt of retirement pension
class_z.notes: Confirmed by the founder: a retiree drawing NIS pension who returns to work pays the reduced Class Z rate. It buys employment-injury cover only — no further retirement benefit accrues, which is why it is ~5%.

benefit_rates._rule: SINGLE CURRENT TABLE, applied at QUALIFICATION date — NOT era-selected like contributions. NIBTT's own wording proves it: 'Rates ... for persons qualifying on or after 7th January 2008.'
benefit_rates._critical_warning: NIBTT PUBLISHES BENEFIT RATES IN TWO PLACES WITH DIFFERENT VALUES AND DOES NOT RECONCILE THEM. The Benefits section (/benefits_09/tables/retire_invalidity_rates.htm) serves a STALE 2008 table and is the one its own Retirement pages link to. The CURRENT table lives under /Contribution_Rates/. Always use the 2016 table.

current.title: Basic Retirement and Invalidity Pension Rates 2016

superseded_2008.warning: THE PUBLIC CALCULATORS CURRENTLY HOLD THESE VALUES. They understate the pension ~40%, which OVERSTATES the retirement gap, which sells more product. That is the self-serving direction, wearing the client's own authority in a self-serve model. THIS IS THE PRIORITY FIX.
superseded_2008._history_note: The 2014 Benefit Tables PDF prints 2013 and 2014 side by side; its 2013 column equals this table exactly, proving the 2008 rates ran through 2013. Progression Class I monthly: 335.83 (2008-13) -> 419.79 (2014) -> 566.72 (2016).

increments._problem: The 2016 table publishes BASICS ONLY — no increment column. The 2013 table (benefits_09/tables/2013/retire_invalidity_rates.htm) publishes INCREMENTS ONLY. NIBTT appears to publish only what changed in each revision.

readings.a: 2013 increments still stand — 2014 and 2016 revised only basics. Current = 2016 basics + 2013 increments.
readings.b: Increments were revised in 2016 but not published on the site.

increments.warning: DO NOT GUESS. Reading (a) fits the publish-only-what-changed pattern, but this project has twice been burned by a plausible inference. Confirm with NIBTT directly or from the Legal Notices (Amendments/NIBTTAct_amend.html, Legal Notices 25-30) before the pension formula ships.
increments.engine_behaviour: Until resolved: compute the BASIC pension and the minimum, and REFUSE to compute increments rather than guess. Surface 'increment value unconfirmed' rather than silently using 2013.

formula.source: NIBTT retirement pages + NIBTT training transcript

averaging_basis.quote: the manner in which we calculate the averages. Do you guys understand that it's not based on your last value of contributions, but your average value throughout your lifetime?
averaging_basis.warning: NOT final salary. NOT last 7 years. The '7 years' rule people remember is a QUALIFYING condition (employed 5 of the last 7 years), not the averaging window. Two different rules — implement both, separately.

pension.note: may include paid, Voluntary, Age Credits and/or Benefit Credits — not just paid weeks

value.alternative_a: 150 total contributions with 50 in the last 3 years

minimum_pension.quote: The board shall pay with effect from February 1, 2012 the sum of $3,000.00 monthly, as a pension to each person qualifying for a Retirement Pension
minimum_pension.notes: Applies only to persons QUALIFYING for a Retirement Pension (750+ contributions). Unindexed since 2012 — the 9th Actuarial Review explicitly recommended holding it there. Binds for classes I-XII; XIII-XVI now exceed it on basics alone. A challenge claiming the minimum attaches to the GRANT rather than the PENSION was refuted 0-3.

retirement_grant.value: 3 x monetary value of total contributions
retirement_grant.notes: For persons with FEWER than 750 contributions. Excluded from SCP assessed income (not monthly income).

claim_rules.60_to_64: must cease insurable employment to claim; may return to insurable employment before 65 and keep the pension
claim_rules.65: payable whether or not the person retires

scp._regulator: Ministry of the People, Social Development and Family Services

bands.warning: Income must not exceed 5,500/month — above that is a HARD DISQUALIFICATION, not a taper to zero. NOTE: this rests on ONE Ministry page. An earlier verification round refuted these exact bands 1-2 before the source was scraped. A second source would be welcome.
bands.form_discrepancy: The linked SCP application form (2020) still states income must not exceed $4,500. The maintained page says $5,500. Prefer the page over the PDF.

assessed_income_includes_nis_pension.evidence: Application form requires 'Evidence of National Insurance Benefits / other Pension / Benefits' (item 6) and asks 'Are you a Government or other pensioner? If so, how much is your monthly pension?' (item 31).
excludes: one-time NIS Retirement Grant (not monthly income)
assessed_income_includes_nis_pension.notes: Confirmed by the founder. An earlier research round declared this unanswerable; the answer was on the Ministry's own form.

eligibility.residency: 20 years immediately preceding the claim (absences not exceeding 5 years in aggregate) OR 50 years in aggregate (not necessarily consecutive)
eligibility.basis: s.4(1) Senior Citizens' Pension Act Chap. 32:02

cliff_edges.warning: Hard thresholds. At 5,501 assessed income SCP goes to ZERO — one extra dollar costs 500/month. The engine MUST refuse to land a client just over a cliff without flagging it.
cliff_edges.modal_case: No NIS -> SCP 3,500 -> total 3,500. NIS minimum 3,000 -> SCP 2,500 -> total 5,500. A 3,000 NIS pension delivers 2,000. Since classes I-XII land at the 3,000 minimum, this is the COMMON case, not an edge case. Note SCP's maximum (3,500) EXCEEDS the NIS minimum pension (3,000).

statutory_maturity_floor.basis: Income Tax Act — an approved pension fund plan or approved deferred annuity plan cannot provide for retirement or maturity before age 50
statutory_maturity_floor.engine_rule: REFUSE to model maturity below 50 — it is not legal, not merely disadvantageous.

exemption_window.basis: s.8(1)(ta) ITA, inserted by Finance Act 2026 cl.21(a)
exemption_window.engine_rule: WARN (do not refuse) when a proposed annuity maturity exceeds 70 — legal, but forfeits the exemption. NOTE: this rule cannot fire on a Registered Destiny, whose only maturity options are 50/55/60/65/70. It matters for Unregistered.

income_exemption.basis: Act No. 16 of 2026 (Finance Act 2026), assented 2026-06-25, gazetted 2026-06-29, Gazette Vol. 65 No. 111

s8_1_ta_annuity.applies_to: approved deferred annuity plan under s.28
conditions: purchased by an individual resident in Trinidad and Tobago
matures between the ages of fifty and seventy

s8_1_tb_pension_fund.applies_to: approved pension fund plan under s.28, upon maturity
s8_1_tb_pension_fund.warning: NO AGE WINDOW. The two exemptions are DIFFERENT SHAPES. A planner treating them alike will get one wrong.

retroactive_scope.value: applies to plans approved BEFORE, ON, or AFTER 2026-01-01
retroactive_scope.commercial_note: The exemption is NOT limited to new business. Every approved annuity already on the book falls inside the new treatment if it meets the conditions. This is a review trigger across the whole book.

early_surrender_tax.basis: s.28(10) Income Tax Act — obliges a trustee/trust corporation/company to deduct or withhold
early_surrender_tax.warning: The 25% CANNOT be cited to s.28(9). Finance Act 2026 cl.21(c) replaced s.28(9) with a bare avoidance-of-doubt provision specifying NO rate: 'any sum received when an approved pension fund plan or an approved deferred annuity plan is surrendered before the date of retirement or maturity shall be subject to tax.'
early_surrender_tax.notes: Only premiums refunded; accumulated gains forfeited; BIR approval required for surrender.

bir_approval_required.notes: Approved vs non-approved must be a first-class distinction in the data model. Only BIR-approved annuities qualify for the deduction and the exemption.

s134_6a_deferred_compensation.basis: NOT read from the statute. Three independent implementations agree on the shape: the greater of one-third of chargeable income, or 20% of gross emoluments.
sources: Tatil Cashbuilder III Product Specification (1995) — 'The maximum premium is one-third of the chargeable income of the employee.'

Sagicor Business Tax Secure Annuity Plan (live, retrieved 2026-08-11) — 'up to 1/3 of assessable income or 20% of the employee's gross income (whichever is greater)', stated to operate under s.134(6).
s134_6a_deferred_compensation.basis_of_the_fraction: CHARGEABLE income. Confirmed 2026-08-11 by the practitioner from his own quotation practice, and consistent with the 1995 Tatil spec and the live calculator. Sagicor's marketing page says 'assessable', which is the looser (larger) reading; it is not followed here. Chargeable is net of all deductions, so this is both the confirmed and the conservative basis.
s134_6a_deferred_compensation.warning: Employer-owned and employer-funded, so it FAILS the 'purchased by an individual who is a resident' condition in s.8(1)(ta). Income from a s.134(6) plan is therefore NOT covered by the Finance Act 2026 maturity exemption. Source: ATTIC guidance reported in the Trinidad Express, 2026. Do not present s.134(6) as a strictly larger version of a personal registered annuity — the deduction is bigger, the maturity treatment is worse.
open_questions: Is the employer's contribution a taxable benefit to the employee? The e-Tax return carries a line 'Employer's contribution to Fund (Taxable Benefit)', so it is for SOME funds. Unresolved for s.134(6).
No statutory text located. Do not cite a subsection to a client on this basis.
Lead for both: the 52pp 'Corporation Tax Training' document.
conditions: Employer owns the policy and is the applicant; employer takes the deduction against corporation tax
Each policy must be BIR-approved before issue
Cannot be borrowed against, assigned or surrendered (BIR conditions for deductibility)

estate_tax.notes: T&T has NO inheritance, estate, or gift taxes. Estate duty repealed.

capital_gains_tax.notes: Do not import US/AU estate-liquidity or CGT planning framings — they do not apply here.

estate.engine_rule: OMIT the US estate-tax liquidity driver from the needs formula. The T&T estate pitch is PROBATE BYPASS and asset titling/succession (Succession Act Ch. 9:02), not liquidity for tax. Optional: a stamp-duty calculator for gifts/conveyances.

conventions._note: T&T market conventions — local norms, not universal truths. Sourced from the standard fact-finding instruments.

rental_income_months.source: Tatil Life Client Financial Profile (needs formula)

income_continuation_to_age.source: Tatil Life Client Financial Profile — 'Continuation of Income until Last child attains age 21'

emergency_fund_multiple.notes: Note: 6x GROSS INCOME, not months of expenses as in US convention.

benchmark_allocation.source: Identical across PALIG Personal Net Worth Calculator (2012) and Maritime Financial Fact Finder
benchmark_allocation.notes: Two independent T&T insurers, thirteen years apart, identical. This is convention, not house style.

budget_bands.unit: fraction of income toward solving needs
budget_bands.notes: Elicit budget as a PERCENTAGE BAND with this social-proof anchor, not as a dollar figure. The middle band reads as the norm, the top flatters, the bottom gives permission.
